newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends down, eroded by A share loss.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends down, eroded by A share loss.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Friday in line with the A share market on talk that Beijing was planning measures to cool the markets down, brokers said.
The B share index slipped 1.34 points or 0.84 percent to close at 157.34 on turnover of HK$72.83 million compared with Thursday's HK$64.56 million.
The A index slid 7.90 points or 1.71 percent to 453.62 on turnover of 9.55 billion yuan against 10.67 billion in the previous session.
"B shares were dragged down by the A shares which were hurt by talk that Beijing was drafting anti-speculation measures," a trader with Shenzhen J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.

Earlier this week, China's main securities newspapers warned investors that there was a danger of the markets overheating and called for more risk control. Shenzhen's A share market has risen more than 40 percent since the beginning of the year.
"Buying interest is low as we move towards the end of the corporate reporting season," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities. "The bearishness is going to extend into early next week."
"Disappointing dividend plans by some B share firms also contributed to the day's retreat," an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services in Shenzhen said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao was the worst performer on the B share market, diving HK$0.30 or 6.82 percent to HK$4.10 on volume of 28,300 shares.
Guangdong Electric Power traded the most on 1.57 million shares and closed up HK$0.08 at HK$7.68 after the firm announced solid 1996 results.
